text.en: Raju read that a steel plant uses coal and iron. "Where do these come from?" he asked.

Natural resources come from nature and can include materials, living things, and sources of energy. Minerals include iron ore, coal, bauxite and mica, and power resources include coal, petroleum, natural gas, water and the sun and wind. Coal and petroleum are non-renewable. Solar and wind energy are renewable. Conventional and non-conventional describe different histories of use and are not the same classification.
Manufacturing industries can be classified by their main inputs. Cotton textiles and sugar are agro-based. Iron and steel and cement are mineral-based. Information technology is a service. Industries cluster near raw material, power and markets.
Tamil Nadu is known for cotton textiles at Coimbatore and Tiruppur, automobile industries around Chennai and leather at Vellore. Mines like lignite at Neyveli feed power plants.
Natural resources are materials, living things or energy sources from nature that people can use.
Minerals include iron ore, coal, bauxite and mica, and power resources include coal, petroleum, natural gas, water and the sun and wind.

Renewable resources are replenished on human timescales. Sun and wind are examples. Coal is non-renewable. Conventional and non-conventional describe historical patterns of use, rather than how quickly a resource returns.
Manufacturing activities can be classified by their main inputs. Cotton textiles are agro-based, while iron and steel and cement are mineral-based. Information technology is a service activity.
Industries cluster near raw material, power and markets.
Tamil Nadu is known for cotton textiles at Coimbatore and Tiruppur, automobile industries around Chennai and leather at Vellore.
Mines like lignite at Neyveli feed power plants.
A material becomes useful as a resource when people can use it. Its value may depend on technology, labour and transport.
A mineral is a naturally occurring substance. An ore contains material from which something valuable can be recovered economically.

board.text: A mineral and an ore are different ideas

text.en: Rock type and geological history affect where deposits occur. A region can have rich deposits of one mineral and few of another.
Iron ore supplies material for iron and steel. Bauxite is a major source of aluminium. These are examples of ores with different uses.
Limestone is an important input for cement. Mica is another example of a non-metallic mineral.
Coal and lignite are fossil fuels. Lignite occurs at Neyveli, where it has been used as a fuel for generating electricity.

board.text: Coal and lignite have stored energy

text.en: Oil and gas can provide energy or materials for manufactured products. Their deposits are limited because they form very slowly.

board.text: Petroleum and natural gas have several uses

text.en: Sunlight and wind continue on human timescales. A coal deposit does not recover on the timescale of mining.
Moving water can turn a turbine to generate electricity. The water cycle renews the supply, while river flow and reservoir effects still matter.
Solar output changes between day and night, and wind power depends on local wind conditions. Electricity systems plan for changes in output.

board.text: Wind and sunlight vary by time and place

text.en: Efficient use and recycling can reduce demand for new material. Restoring land after extraction can help reduce long-term damage.

board.text: Responsible resource use looks beyond extraction

text.en: Manufacturing takes materials such as cotton, cane or minerals and turns them into useful goods.
Cotton textiles depend on cotton as a main input. Sugar mills process sugar cane, another agricultural product.

board.text: Agro-based industries begin with farm products

text.en: Iron and steel production uses iron-bearing ore. Cement production uses materials such as limestone.

board.text: Mineral-based industries depend on mineral inputs

text.en: A factory may consider the cost of bringing in inputs, moving goods out, employing workers and using reliable power.

board.text: Industrial location depends on several costs

text.en: When materials are costly to haul, factories may locate near mines or major transport routes. This does not determine every location.

board.text: Heavy inputs and bulky outputs make transport important

text.en: A group of firms in one area can share suppliers, repair services, skilled workers and transport connections.

board.text: An industrial cluster links nearby businesses

text.en: Cotton may come from outside a textile centre. Spinning, knitting, finishing and selling can take place at different sites connected by transport.

board.text: Textile work can span several locations

text.en: Factories and component suppliers around Chennai show how a large industry can draw on roads, ports and specialised workers.
These places are associated with parts of textile production. A place can specialise in only some stages of the full supply chain.

board.text: Coimbatore and Tiruppur illustrate textile clusters

text.en: Jobs and services can grow around factories. Water demand, waste and pollution can also affect local people and environments.
Ask what the factory needs and where the output will go. Compare material, labour, energy, transport and environmental effects.

board.text: Use evidence to compare possible sites

text.en: A region can have mining, manufacturing and services at the same time. The categories describe what particular activities do.

board.text: One region can have several kinds of activity

problem.en: Why are solar and wind called renewable?

text.en: They are not used up.
They come from nature again and again.
They cause little pollution.

problem.en: Why is a sugar mill described as agro-based?

text.en: Identify its main input as sugar cane.

why.en: Sugar cane is an agricultural product.

text.en: The mill converts this crop into a manufactured product.

why.en: The industry’s category reflects its main raw material.

problem.en: How might two factories in the same area benefit from specialised suppliers?

text.en: Both can obtain parts or repairs from nearby businesses.

why.en: This can shorten travel and reduce delays.

text.en: Their concentration can support a wider supplier and worker network.

why.en: That is one benefit of an industrial cluster.

problem.en: Why can wind energy be renewable even when a turbine produces little on a calm day?

text.en: Renewable refers to the continued supply of wind over time.

why.en: It does not mean output is constant.

text.en: Weather changes the power available at a particular moment.

why.en: A renewable resource can still vary.

prompt.en: A friend says Coal is a renewable resource. How will you reply?
